1) the development of a depletion zone is a general phenomenon for protein crystallization, 2) this phenomenon is not affected by microgravity, 3) the depletion zone is not a stable structure, and 4) the stability of the zone depends on the presence of residual acceleration and/or g-jitters.

the use of microgravity for growing protein single crystals has not yet proved to be advantageous, and that the main problem to overcome is not the presence of gravity itself, but its residual effects.
